citation: Xu H. et al., Control of the Nucleation Density of Molybdenum Disulfide in Large-Scale Synthesis Using Chemical Vapor Deposition, Materials 11(6):870 (2018)
system: Tube furnace CVD, MoO3 + S powders, SiO2/Si, MoO3 at 550-700 C, S at 180 C
observed_magnitude: 0.0061 N/um2 at 10 sccm to 0.2912 N/um2 at 160 sccm (peak); decreases above 160 sccm
quote: While the gas flow rate was 10 sccm, the nucleation density of MoS2 was 0.0061 N/μm2. ... nucleation density reached the top value of 0.2912 N/μm2
notes: Non-monotonic: density falls again above 160 sccm (attributed to insufficient S vapour). Paper text has an inconsistent flow range (10-240 vs 160-280 sccm). Quote assembled from two nearby sentences; quote text relayed via page extraction, not re-checked in a browser.

system: Same as s01; substrate placed at different positions across the flow-velocity distribution
quote: The triangular side of the largest domain reached up to 7 μm. ... The side length of the largest triangular domain is about 15 μm.
notes: Position is a lateral coordinate in a flow-velocity profile, not distance from MoO3; local flow velocity and MoO3 concentration both vary with x. At x=0.1 mm only small nuclei formed.

citation: Prasad R.K., Singh D.K., Continuous Large Area Monolayered Molybdenum Disulfide Growth Using Atmospheric Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition, ACS Omega 8(12):10930 (2023)
system: Single-zone APCVD, 15 mg MoO3 + 200 mg S, 750 C, 5 min, source-substrate 19 cm
observed_magnitude: ~80 um at 50 sccm to ~7 um at 300 sccm
quote: Growth with 50 sccm of argon flow results in MoS2 flakes having a large crystallite size of ∼80 μm ... 300 sccm results in MoS2 crystallites of size as small as ∼7 μm
notes: Quote joined from two sentences. Same flow series also raised layer number at 250/300 sccm.

citation: Prasad R.K., Singh D.K., ACS Omega 8(12):10930 (2023)
quote: A gas flow rate of 100 sccm results in a coverage area of 70% while a flow rate of 150 sccm leads to 92% coverage area
notes: The ~40% value for 50 sccm was relayed by the page extraction and not verified verbatim. Coverage increases while domain size decreases (trade-off, see s03). Peak at intermediate flow.

citation: Prasad R.K., Singh D.K., ACS Omega 8(12):10930 (2023)
system: Same as s03, Ar flow fixed, 200 mg S
observed_magnitude: 10 mg: multilayer; 15, 20, 25 mg: monolayer; 30 mg: bilayer; 10 mg crystallites ~7 um
quote: Raman spectra of 10 mg MoO3 grown samples shows the multilayer growth formation ... with 15, 20, and 25 mg of MoO3 indicated monolayer growth. While growth with 30 mg of MoO3 indicates bilayer growth.
notes: Non-monotonic in MoO3 amount (multilayer at low and high ends). Quote joined from adjacent sentences.

citation: Prasad R.K., Singh D.K., ACS Omega 8(12):10930 (2023)
observed_magnitude: 200 mg: ~30 um and continuous film (few mm2); 400 mg: ~7 um
quote: Doubling the sulfur amount to 200 mg results in a crystallite size of ∼30 μm and continuous film upto few mm2
notes: Non-monotonic: 400 mg reduced crystallite size to ~7 um (sentence relayed via extraction). The 100 mg size is not recorded here.

citation: Tummala P.P. et al., Application-Oriented Growth of a Molybdenum Disulfide (MoS2) Single Layer by Means of Parametrically Optimized Chemical Vapor Deposition, Materials 13(12):2786 (2020)
system: CVD with MoO3 + S, 760 torr, 10 min-class growth, SiO2/Si
observed_magnitude: 650: isolated triangles; 700: high density; 750: coalesced monolayer; 800: 3D islands on monolayer
quote: At this temperature, MoS2 domains with a large area coalesce so as to form a continuous monolayer. ... Increasing the temperature to 800 °C resulted in the formation of 3D islands on a continuous monolayer.
notes: Non-monotonic optimum at 750 C. Quotes relayed via page extraction.

observed_magnitude: 2 mm: ~7-8 layer bulk-like; 5 mm: plume of bulk deposition with thin edge; 10 mm: uniform mono-/bilayer
quote: a 10 mm vertical gap is the best favorable condition to obtain uniformly continuous
notes: Quote is a truncated fragment as relayed; the 2 mm and 5 mm descriptions are paraphrased from the extraction. Layer number decreases with larger gap.

citation: Wang S., Pacios M., Bhaskaran H., Warner J.H., Substrate control for large area continuous films of monolayer MoS2 by atmospheric pressure chemical vapor deposition, Nanotechnology 27:085604 (2016); read via Oxford ORA accepted manuscript
system: Two-furnace APCVD, MoO3 + S, SiO2/Si, growth temp 750 C
change: 200 C to 400 C (growth temp fixed at 750 C)
observed_magnitude: qualitative: higher nucleation density, smaller grains, island-like
quote: when increasing the heating temperature of MoO3 from 200°C to 400°C, the MoS2 nucleation density goes up with a deterioration in the uniformity of the layer thickness, leading to island-like structures with smaller grain sizes
notes: DOI inferred from the Nanotechnology 27:085604 reference and not confirmed; verify. Text read from the ORA PDF.

observed_magnitude: qualitative: lower nucleation density, larger triangular monolayer domains
quote: when the MoO3 temperature is fixed with a rise in the growth temperature, the nucleation density decreases with improved homogeneity in the layer thickness and higher crystallinity
notes: Numeric growth temperature range not extracted. Direction of nucleation density is the outcome; domain size increases. DOI unconfirmed as in s09.

citation: Wang L. et al., Enhanced chemical vapour deposition of monolayer MoS2 films via a clean promoter, arXiv:2502.04505 (2025)
system: Tube furnace CVD, MoO3 at 835 C, N2 carrier, S heated by separate belt; flake data from the promoter region
observed_magnitude: shape hexagonal rounded (180 C, ~3-4 um) to triangular (200-250 C); promoter-region mean size 9.8 um (250 C), 11.2 um (270 C), ~4 um (300 C)
quote: In the promoter region, the average flake size is approximately 4 μm at 180 °C and increases with the sulphur temperature, reaching a peak of 9.8 μm at 250 °C and 11.2 μm at 270 °C.
notes: Non-monotonic: size drops back to ~4 um at 300 C. Data are for a promoter-treated region; pristine region stays 3-5 um at all temperatures. Promoter-region result may not transfer to plain MoO3/S growth. Text read from the PDF.

citation: Withanage S.S. et al., Uniform Vapor-Pressure-Based Chemical Vapor Deposition Growth of MoS2 Using MoO3 Thin Film as a Precursor for Coevaporation, ACS Omega 3(12):18943 (2018)
system: Face-down CVD with thermally evaporated MoO3 thin film + S powder
quote: the crystal sizes are reduced at lower thicknesses of MoO3 because of the low-precursor supply.
notes: Quote lightly truncated at start by the extraction. Precursor is a thin film, not powder.

citation: Withanage S.S. et al., ACS Omega 3(12):18943 (2018)
system: Same as s12, 20 nm MoO3 film
observed_magnitude: qualitative; multilayer growth at nucleation centres at higher T
quote: We also found that the coverage density generally decreases at higher growth temperatures.
notes: Sits with s07/s10: temperature effects depend on setup and whether growth is mass-transport or kinetically limited.

citation: Najmaei S. et al., Vapor phase growth and grain boundary structure of molybdenum disulfide atomic layers, Nature Materials 12:754 (2013); read via arXiv:1301.2812
system: CVD with dispersed MoO3 nanoribbons + S powder, SiO2/Si, 850 C, 550 C source heating
change: varied density of dispersed MoO3 nanoribbons, all else constant
observed_magnitude: qualitative: isolated triangles to partial film to continuous monolayer film as precursor supply and nucleation density increase
quote: varying the density of dispersed nanoribbons systematically slows or stops the growth at certain points
notes: Paper states the series is diffusion-limited by MoO3-x vapour. Journal DOI recalled, not confirmed in text read. Qualitative only.
